beats.text: Saying hello to Voyager 1 now takes a full day.
beats.header: Voyager 1 · one light-day from Earth (18 Nov 2026)
beats.anchor: a radio message needs 24 hours, one way

beats.text: It launched in nineteen seventy-seven and has been coasting outward ever since, at about seventeen kilometres every second.
beats.anchor: New York to London in 5½ minutes

beats.text: One light-day is about twenty-six billion kilometres, a hundred and seventy-three times farther out than the Sun.
beats.anchor: 173 trips from Earth to the Sun

beats.text: Its transmitter runs on about twenty watts, roughly a fridge light bulb, and seventy-metre dishes on Earth still catch it.
beats.anchor: about one fridge bulb of power

beats.text: Its plutonium power shrinks every year, so engineers keep switching instruments off; only two of ten still run.
beats.anchor: a few watts less every year

beats.text: And every day it drifts one and a half million kilometres farther from the Sun, which means
beats.header: Earth seen by Voyager 1, 1990 · +1.5M km a day
beats.anchor: about four Earth–Moon trips a day
